plain_english_revision: The amendment clarifies and strengthens the original bill's provisions to ensure that Bible-related elective courses in Alabama public schools are academically rigorous, optional for all students, and temporary in their display of artifacts/symbols. It also mandates that curriculum standards for these courses meet state-approved benchmarks for other electives.
candidate_position_supported: Ensuring Bible-related elective courses in public schools are academically rigorous, optional, and temporary in their display of artifacts/symbols while aligning with state curriculum standards for other electives.
evidence_quotes: including a requirement that curriculum standards submitted by a public school or school district for approval of an elective study of the Bible course shall meet the academic rigor and curriculum standards of other elective courses approved by the state board
and is displayed only throughout the duration the course

The local board of education shall ensure all students in each grade for which courses are offered under this section have the option to take elective courses and meet all grade-level requirements without taking a course under this section.
review_reason: The amendment text is clear, specific, and does not rely on unseen language or procedural ambiguity. The changes are affirmative policy adjustments to the original bill's provisions.
